question: A vector $\vec{a}$ has magnitude $12$ and is directed along the direction ratios $2,-1,2$. Determine $\vec{a}$, obtain its direction cosines, and establish the scalar and directional relationship between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}=12\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$.
explanation: Obtaining the Required DirectionA vector having direction ratios $2,-1,2$ is parallel to`\vec{d}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}`The magnitude of $\vec{d}$ is`|\vec{d}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+2^2}=3`Therefore, the unit vector in this direction is`\hat{d}=\frac{1}{3}(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})`Applying the Given MagnitudeSince $\vec{a}$ has magnitude $12$,`\vec{a}=12\hat{d}\vec{a}=4(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\vec{a}=8\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+8\hat{k}`The direction cosines are the components of the corresponding unit vector. Hence,`l=\frac{2}{3},\qquad m=-\frac{1}{3},\qquad n=\frac{2}{3}`They satisfy`l^2+m^2+n^2=\frac{4}{9}+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{4}{9}=1`Establishing the Vector RelationshipFor the given vector $\vec{b}$,`\vec{b}=12\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+12\hat{k}`Comparing it with $\vec{a}$ gives`\vec{b}=\frac{3}{2}\vec{a}`Since the scalar multiplier $\frac{3}{2}$ is positive, the vectors are parallel and have the same direction. Also,`|\vec{b}|=\frac{3}{2}|\vec{a}|=18`Final ResultThe vector is $\vec{a}=8\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$, its direction cosines are $\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}$, and $\vec{b}=\frac{3}{2}\vec{a}$.

options.B: $\vec{a}=8\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$; direction cosines $\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}$; $\vec{b}=\frac{3}{2}\vec{a}$, so they are parallel with the same direction and $|\vec{b}|=18$.
options.D: $\vec{a}=8\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$; direction cosines $\frac{2}{3},-\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}$; $\vec{b}=-\frac{3}{2}\vec{a}$, so they have opposite directions.
